And through this — it is considered as if each one of Israel fulfilled all the mitzvos of the Torah — since he includes himself with all Israel in the faith of unity — which is the foundation of everything. And also: one who grasps a part of the unity — it is as if he grasps the whole — as is brought. Ben Nannas says: the verse ve-ahavta le-re'acha kamokha is the most comprehensive. For from this it is seen in actual sensory experience — the unity among Israel. And this one fulfills this mitzvah — and this one fulfills this mitzvah — and it is considered as if each one fulfilled all of them. Ben Pazi says: the verse "the one lamb" is the most comprehensive. For from this it is seen even more in sensory experience — that all Israel are like one man — and are atoned each day by one lamb in the morning and in the evening. And this is what he said: the law follows Ben Pazi — which is also along this path. For each one of Israel is obligated to make a sanctuary for the dwelling of His Shechinah, blessed be He. And in that each one has some portion in the Tabernacle — it is considered as if he himself built the entire Tabernacle — and the Holy One Blessed be He causes His Shechinah to rest in him. And not only that — but on the contrary — specifically through the Tabernacle being built from the generous donation of the heart of all Israel — through this specifically the Holy One Blessed be He dwells in it — as it is written: "and they shall make for Me a sanctuary" — that all of them shall make one sanctuary — specifically. For all Israel together are one complete stature and one unity, as stated above. And so too regarding the fulfillment of mitzvos as well, as stated above.

 
 Sichot HaRan, Siman 55 · סימן נ"ה

 Me-Inyan Tov Olam HaBa — "Regarding the Good of the World to Come"

Eretz Yisrael is a foretaste of the World to Come — as stated above many times. And whoever walks even four cubits in Eretz Yisrael — it is assured for him that he is a son of the World to Come. Therefore it is written of her: "the land is very very good." For in truth — to call Eretz Yisrael merely good — is not sufficient — for she is far far above even the aspect of good — like a foretaste of the World to Come. And similarly very good — was also said of all of Creation in general — "and G-d saw all that He had made — and behold it was very good." But Eretz Yisrael is above even the aspect of very good. Only she is in the aspect of: "the land is very very good" — meaning: without measure and comparison at all.

 
 Sichot HaRan, Siman 87 · סימן פ"ז

 Lipi Bechinas HaYomim Nora'im — "According to the Aspect of the Days of Awe"

It has already been explained above many times that the primary wisdom is in Eretz Yisrael. And therefore there is the primary beauty and splendor — as it is written: "beautiful in loftiness," etc. — and it is written: "from Tzion — the perfection of beauty," etc. And our Sages said: "there is no beauty like the beauty of Yerushalayim." And it is in the aspect of: "you are all beautiful, my beloved — there is no blemish in you." For there is no deficiency in her — as it is written: "it lacks nothing." And all of this is because of the wisdom within her — the aspect of: "the wisdom of a person illuminates his face." And our Sages said: "you acquired knowledge — what do you lack?" And this is the aspect of: "and you shall honor the face of the elder." An elder — this is one who has acquired wisdom. But even so — the primary perfection of the wisdom within her is through simplicity and straightforwardness — which one merits there — the aspect of: "and the wholehearted shall remain in it," as stated above. And this simplicity — meaning: one removes all the wisdoms — and serves the Holy One Blessed be He in simplicity — this is the aspect of drawing the mind that is in the da'as to the very bones. And from there flows the adornment of the esrog — which is itself the aspect of the adornment and beauty of the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael — which is the aspect of Malchus — as stated above many times. And see in Likutay Halachos — Laws of Yom Kippur, halachah 2 — it is explained more fully there.

 And this is what is written [Mishlei 3]: "do not be wise in your own eyes — fear Hashem and turn from evil — it will be healing for your navel and refreshment for your bones." For through this — that one draws the wisdom and the mind to the da'as — to be in simplicity — fearing Hashem and turning from evil — this is a refreshing drink for his bones — the aspect of: "and his bones' marrow will be moistened" — as is explained within the ma'amar. And this simplicity is the aspect of: "and behold the lad was weeping" — the aspect of: "for Israel was a lad — and I loved him." Love is the aspect of the sukkah — the aspect of the right, etc. — this being the aspect of the conquest of Eretz Yisrael — which was through Yehoshua — who is called a lad — as it is written: "and Yehoshua the son of Nun — a lad." And similarly the spies that Yehoshua sent to scout Eretz Yisrael — it is written of them: "and the lads the spies came." And similarly Dovid — who completed the conquest of Eretz Yisrael — it is written: "a lad — ruddy" — and it is written [Shmuel I 17]: "whose son is this lad?", etc. And similarly of Shlomoh it is written [Divray HaYomim I 29]: "a tender lad."

 And this is what is written [Zechariyah 2]: "and he said to him: run and speak to this lad — saying: Yerushalayim shall be inhabited as open towns — because of the multitude of men and animals within it," etc. For through this aforementioned simplicity — which is the aspect of a weeping lad — all the building of Yerushalayim depends on this — the aspect of: "with weeping they shall come," etc. And this itself is the aspect of: "man and animal" — as our Sages expounded: "'man and animal You save, Hashem' — these are human beings who are cunning in their way — yet even as they grow old — they do not depart from it." Meaning: that one must educate the human being in the path of the simplicity and straightforwardness of holiness — so greatly — this being the aspect of the lad — until he does not depart from the path of holy simplicity even when he grows old. And this is the aspect of: "elders together with lads shall praise the Name of Hashem" — and our Sages expounded in the Midrash [Shocher Tov, Tehillim]: "elders who are like lads — as it is written: 'He will renew your youth like the eagle'" — as stated above. For even when one merits to complete wisdom — which is the aspect of holy old age — even so — one walks in the paths of simplicity. This being the aspect of: "for Israel was a lad." And through this very thing they renew themselves in the service of Hashem every time more and more.

And this is what is placed adjacent in Siman 51 — (in the discourse that begins: the World to Come is nothing): also wisdoms are nothing — only simplicity and straightforwardness. And also in simplicity one must not be a fool — (for this is the aspect of a literal lad — who does acts of childishness and foolishness — and of this it is said: "woe to you, O land — whose king is a lad." And as we find regarding Rechavam — who erred greatly in this — having gone after the counsel of the lads) — but even so — wisdoms are not needed at all. And also it is not good to be old, etc. — only to renew oneself every day, etc. — as stated above. And therefore the blind old man in the story of the seven beggars said of himself: "I am very old — and yet I am completely young," etc. And see in Likutay Halachos — Laws of Tefillin, halachah 5. And this is the aspect of: "I was a lad — and I have also grown old." And this is what our Sages said [Shabbos 88a]: "why is Israel compared to an apple — what a tappuach?" — the Tosafos explained: this means an esrog — "just as the apple [esrog] — its fruit precedes its leaves — so too Israel — they preceded na'aseh [we will do] to nishma [we will hear]." And placed adjacent to it is the question of the heretic who asked Rava regarding na'aseh ve-nishma. And he replied to him: "we who walk in wholesomeness" — Rashi explained: "we walked with Him in innocent-heartedness," etc. — "as it is written: 'the wholesomeness of the upright shall guide them.'" The paths of holy simplicity — this being the aspect of the adornment of the esrog, as stated above. And this is the primary pride and beauty of holiness of Israel — as it is written: "she is unique — my dove — my wholehearted one" — meaning: the aspect of this simplicity. And this is: "I am dark" — meaning: from the language of childhood and darkness — which Rashi explained: youth. And: "and pleasant" — meaning: specifically — through my removing all my wisdom — which is the aspect of the beauty and whiteness of holiness — the aspect of the supernal whiteness — which is the aspect of the whiteness of the hair of the elders — an elder — this is one who has acquired wisdom — as stated above. And through my removing my wisdom and serving Hashem in simplicity — this being the aspect of darkness and obscurity — the aspect of the absence of da'as — this being the aspect of: "I am dark — specifically — therefore — pleasant." For from there is the primary beauty and splendor, as stated above. And this is the aspect of what our Sages said: because they said na'aseh ve-nishma — which is the aspect of simplicity, as stated above — the Holy One Blessed be He said: "and they shall take for Me a portion." Meaning: the aspect of: "for Israel was a lad — and I loved him" — as is brought above. What our Sages said: "'and they shall take for Me a portion' — as it is said: 'I have loved you — says Hashem.'" For through simplicity one merits love and will — the aspect of: "whoever is generous in heart" — and: "like water — face to face," etc. And therefore simplicity is called — in the manner of what is said in Parshas Emor: "it shall be wholehearted [tamim] — for acceptance — no blemish shall be in it." This being the aspect of: "you are all beautiful, my beloved — there is no blemish in you." And this is: "it shall be wholehearted — for acceptance." And it is written [Mishlei 11]: "and His will — those who are wholehearted of way." In the manner of what is explained in Siman 32 — that through simplicity and faith one merits will — which is above wisdom. And this is what is also written [ibid. 12]: "and one who acts faithfully — His will." And Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of faith and simplicity — as stated above — therefore it is written of it: "You desired, Hashem, Your land." And it is called a desirable land, as stated above. And this is: "like the apple tree among the trees of the forest — (meaning: the esrog, as stated above) — in its shade I desired and I sat." And therefore the esrog is called from the language of chamid and ragig [desire and longing] — as is known — for it is the fruit of a beautiful tree and lovely to look upon — the aspect of the beauty of the esrog. And this is: "you are beautiful, my beloved — as Tirtzah" — from the language of ratzon [will] — as our Sages said. And the primary is through the simplicity. And this is what our Sages expounded [Menachos 27, Sukkah 37]: "and you shall take for yourselves" — that the taking should be wholehearted — the aspect of this simplicity. And this is what our Sages expounded in the Midrash [Mishlei 30]: "four are smallest of the earth — and they are wise, made wise — regarding the four species of the lulav." For even though they are the aspect of simplicity and straightforwardness — for all the intention of the four species is to draw the mochin and the da'as to the heart — which is the aspect of the esrog — as our Sages said: "the esrog resembles the heart" — this being the aspect of simplicity, as stated above. And as it is written: "may my heart be wholehearted in Your statutes," etc. — and they are in the aspect of: "for Israel was a lad — and I loved him," as stated above — this being the aspect of: smallest of the earth. But even so there is in this specifically great wisdom — for one draws the mochin to the very bones. This being the aspect of: "all my bones shall say," etc. — which our Sages expounded regarding the four species. And this is what our Sages expounded [Sukkah 35]: "the fruit of a beautiful tree" — from the language of making a dwelling [hedir] — just as when the young come — the elders are still present — and there are both the wholehearted and the blemished ones — as stated above. (For one must include the wisdom together with the simplicity — this being the aspect of: elders together with lads — the aspect of: the great ones and the small ones.) And this is: "and there are wholehearted ones and blemished ones in it." For in this simplicity — if it is in holiness and included with the wisdom and the holy mochin — then it is called simplicity — the aspect of: "you are all beautiful, my beloved — there is no blemish in you." But also in simplicity one must not be a fool, as stated above. For there is no greater blemish than this — for: "you lacked knowledge — what did you acquire?" And it has already been explained that Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of simplicity. And this is: "you shall be wholehearted with Hashem your G-d" — the aspect of Eretz Yisrael — for: "one who dwells in Eretz Yisrael — it is as if he has a G-d." And in the manner of what our Rebbe, may his memory be for blessing, explained in the discourse al asher ma'altem — Likutay Moharan Kama, Siman 48. And this is what Moshe prayed: "please — show Your servant," etc. And our Sages said that the initials of: "hadas — lulav — asrog — aravah" spell hillel [praise] — brought in Sha'ar HaChatzair, Siman 231 — as stated above. For through the simplicity symbolized by the four species — one merits Eretz Yisrael. And this is: "please — show Your servant", etc. — as if he had only attained a beginning. And as is explained in Megaleh Amukos, aspect 9 — this being the aspect of: lads together with elders, as stated above.

 
 Sichot HaRan, Siman 85 · סימן פ"ה

 Hafichas HaShulchan — "The Overturning of the Table"

It has already been explained above many times that the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael flows from the aspect of speech — the aspect of: "G-d — Elokim — Hashem — spoke — and He called the earth from Tzion — the perfection of beauty," etc. And Eretz Yisrael itself is the aspect of Malchus peh [Kingdom of the mouth]. And therefore from there the entire flow of livelihood is drawn — the aspect of: "for by every utterance that goes forth from the mouth of Hashem shall man live" — as is explained within the ma'amar. And there is the table — in the aspect of the face. For there shines the light of the face of Hashem — the aspect of: "and the light of Your face — for You favored them." And this is what is placed adjacent [Yehoshua 5]: "and the children of Israel camped in Gilgal — and they made the Passover," etc. (this being the aspect of peh-sach — the mouth that speaks — as is explained within the ma'amar) — "and they ate of the produce of the land from the day after the Passover," etc. For from there the eating that they ate in Eretz Yisrael was drawn. And this is: "and the man ceased from the day after" — in their eating of the produce of the land, etc. For the man was the aspect of the setting of the table in the wilderness — as it is written: "You set before me a table against my oppressors" — and our Sages expounded: regarding the man. And this is the aspect of: "can G-d set a table in the wilderness?" And this is what our Sages expounded: "these forty years," etc., "you lacked nothing — that they lacked only speech. One wanted beef — he would say: let the man become like beef — and it would become so. Saying with his mouth — 'from the man — I want.' 'I will rain down for you bread from the heaven.' Water — I want. 'Behold — he struck the rock and the waters flowed.'" Meaning: for all the livelihood flows from speech, as stated above — therefore they were required to speak at least. And afterwards — when they entered Eretz Yisrael — their eating there was in the aspect of the setting of the table in Eretz Yisrael. And see above — what is explained in Likutay Moharan Kama, Siman 62 — the discourse Vayasev Elokim — and what is brought there in the name of the writings of the Ari, of blessed memory — and you will understand better. And therefore the primary blessing after meals is: "for the land and for the sustenance." For from there the livelihood is drawn in fullness, as stated above. And this is: "I shall walk before Hashem." Halech — walking — is the aspect of livelihood — as in: "dok be-chuchi ve-tishkach be-nagrei" — as is explained in Likutay Moharan Kama, Siman 31 — the discourse bera be-davra. Meaning: that the livelihood and the table should be in the aspect of the face — this is: "in the lands of the living," as stated above. And see also in Megaleh Amukos, aspect 148 and aspect 34.

 
 Sichot HaRan, Siman 89 · סימן פ"ט

 Da She-Yesh — "Know That There Is"

The primary of tzedakah and lovingkindness and compassion is in Eretz Yisrael — as stated above many times. And there the thirteen attributes of compassion shine most greatly — which are the aspect of Arich Anpin — as is known. As is understood in Megaleh Amukos in many places — and as is understood also in the holy Zohar [Parshas Lech, page 79] — which expounded: "and Avram passed through the land" — according to the manner of: "and Hashem passed before him" — and: "and I shall cause all My goodness to pass before you" — that then He revealed to him the thirteen attributes of compassion. And therefore there is the primary length of days — which flows from the aspect of Arich Anpin — as is explained in the Tikkunim. And therefore: "the people that dwells in it — their iniquity is forgiven." For through this the sins are forgiven — the aspect of: "He passes over the first ones first" — as is explained within the ma'amar. And there is the primary rectification — of giving the sins of Edom — as it is written: "and the goat shall carry upon it all their sins," etc. — as our Sages expounded. And therefore when the Bais HaMikdash was destroyed — Asaf prayed: "do not remember against us former iniquities," etc. — as is explained within the ma'amar.

 
 Sichot HaRan, Siman 91 · סימן צ"א

 Segulah Le-Hatmadah — "A Segulah for Persistence"

The sanctity of Eretz Yisrael is well-suited and a most propitious segulah for love of Torah and for persistence — for: "there is no Torah like the Torah of Eretz Yisrael" — and the mochin of Eretz Yisrael are in the aspect of no'am [pleasantness]. Therefore one merits there more to feel the pleasantness and sweetness that is in the Torah — the aspect of: "her ways are ways of pleasantness," etc. And through this one merits persistence — the aspect of: "and all your children shall be disciples of Hashem." And therefore immediately upon entering Eretz Yisrael the angel came and rebuked them about the nullification of Torah. As it is written: "for I am the commander of the army of Hashem — now I have come" — as our Sages expounded: "immediately: 'and Yehoshua went that night in the midst of the valley' — he slept in the depths of the halachah."

 And the primary sanctity of Eretz Yisrael flows from the glorification with which the Holy One Blessed be He glorifies Himself with Israel — as is explained in Likutay Moharan Tanina, Siman 40. Therefore one must especially be careful there — not to speak disparagingly of any one of Israel — and not to find deficiency in any one of Israel — so as not to blemish through this, G-d forbid, in the sanctity of the holy Torah — as is explained within the ma'amar. And similarly in the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael, as stated above. For just as every one of Israel has a grasping in a letter of our holy Torah — so too every one of Israel has a portion in the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael — through the glorification that the Holy One Blessed be He receives from each one of Israel. And this is: "and your people — all of them are righteous — all of them — specifically — as stated above — forever they shall inherit the land."

 
 Sichot HaRan, Siman 93 · סימן צ"ג

Da She-Yesh Ohr — "Know That There Is a Light"

 The sanctity of Eretz Yisrael is in the aspect of the Torah scholar who takes vengeance and bears a grudge — the aspect of: "and the land rises up against him" — as is explained in Likutay Kama, Siman 187. And this is the aspect of: "a land that devours its inhabitants" — as is explained there — and as is brought also in the name of the early ones, of blessed memory. And this is the aspect of: "and the land shall not vomit you out as it vomited out the nation," etc. And therefore: "there is no Torah like the Torah of Eretz Yisrael." For through this aspect — one can divide the thousands into hundreds — and receive the light of the Torah in fullness — the aspect of: "ultimately he will enjoy his learning" — as is explained within the ma'amar. And therefore in the count of the tribes in Parshas Pinchas — there were in every tribe thousands and hundreds. This being the aspect of what they divide the thousands into hundreds — (and as is explained in Likutay Halachos — Laws of Testimony). And placed adjacent immediately to it: "to these shall the land be divided," etc.

 And this is: "a vineyard was Shlomoh's in Baal Hamon" — Rashi explained: in Yerushalayim, etc. And our Sages expounded in the Midrash Shir HaShirim: "a vineyard — these are Israel — as it is said: 'and I brought you to the land of the orchard'" — meaning: to Eretz Yisrael — "a land that Hashem your G-d seeks", etc. — (meaning: the aspect of taking vengeance and bearing a grudge — as our Sages expounded: "that Hashem your G-d seeks it — the Holy One Blessed be He turns it over and over and over," etc. — as is brought). And this is: "and he gave the vineyard to the keepers." For Israel — together with the light of the holy Torah — are one unity. And the Torah scholar who takes vengeance and bears a grudge — can draw the Torah from its root — and lead Israel through it — by dividing the thousands into hundreds, as stated above. And this is: "each man shall bring with his fruit — a thousand of silver." For this light is in the aspect of aleph [a thousand]. And this is: "the thousand is Yours, O Shlomoh." For the Mashiach — who is the aspect of the King whose peace is his — can attain this light as it is in its fullness — in the aspect of thousands. But the rest of the Tzaddikim — they must divide it into hundreds — through being in the aspect of taking vengeance and bearing a grudge, as stated above. And this is: "and two hundred for the keepers of its fruit." And this is what our Sages expounded in the Midrash: "'the thousand is Yours, O Shlomoh' — the master takes a thousand — and the student takes a reward of two hundred", etc., "the master does not take a reward for his learning until he completes it for others" — meaning: he teaches it to others — see Matenot Kehunah. Meaning: even the great master who attains the light in its root — which is in the aspect of aleph — but because the primary perfection of the attainment is to teach it to others — he must therefore necessarily divide it into hundreds for the sake of his students, as stated above. This being the aspect of: "and two hundred for the keepers," etc.

 And this is: "O you who dwell in the gardens — companions hearken to your voice — let me hear." As Rashi explained: "companions — these are the angels," etc. For even the angels long to hear this holy learning — which flows from the aspect of the division of the thousands into hundreds. And so too literally — for the small Tzaddikim receive their vitality from the above. "Flee, my beloved," etc., "upon the mountain of spices" — Rashi explained: Har HaMoriyah and the Bais HaMikdash. For there is the primary drawing of this holy light. And see also in Likutay Halachos — the aforementioned laws — there too the aforementioned verses are brought somewhat briefly. And because one who knows this — can revive the dead — as is explained within the ma'amar — therefore the primary resurrection of the dead will be in Eretz Yisrael — as our Sages said. And this is the aspect of: "your neck is like the tower of Dovid" — Rashi explained: this is the chamber of hewn stone, etc. — "a thousand shields hang upon it." Rashi explained: "like the shield of the thousand — meaning: the Torah," etc. Meaning: for there shines the aforementioned learning — which is in the aspect of aleph. And therefore Shlomoh offered there a thousand burnt-offerings. And this is: "for a day in Your courts is better than a thousand." And therefore learning in general is also called aleph — as in: "lest you learn his paths" — and it is written: "be silent and I will teach you wisdom." And this is: "the craftsmen and the smiths — a thousand" — and as our Sages expounded. And in the future it is written: "and your people — all of them are righteous," etc., "the smallest shall become a thousand," etc. For then this aforementioned light will be drawn — until even the smallest will have attainment through it. And as it is written [Yirmiyahu 31]: "for they shall all know Me — from their smallest to their greatest."

And see in Likutay Halachos — the aforementioned laws — and perhaps one can say that this is what is written in Parshas Matos: "avenge the vengeance of the children of Israel," etc., "afterwards you shall be gathered to your people," etc. For one needs the aspect of taking vengeance and bearing a grudge — in order to concentrate the light and divide the thousands into hundreds. And this is the aspect of the rectification of death and the resurrection of the dead — as is brought within the ma'amar. And this is: "and from the thousands of Israel — a thousand for each tribe," etc. — the aspect of the aforementioned light of the thousands. And this is: "and Moshe was angry at the officers of the army — the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds," etc. And this anger flowed also from the aspect of taking vengeance and bearing a grudge, as stated above. And this is: "commanders of the thousands and commanders of the hundreds." For one must divide the thousands into hundreds. (And this has relevance also to the aspect of bris — as is understood within the ma'amar — for this is the aspect of all the matter of the war that was then against Midyan — because of the matter of Kozbi the daughter of the prince of Midyan, etc. And this is what was commanded in Parshas Pinchas also: "be hostile to the Midyanites," etc. — meaning: to bear them hatred — as Rashi explained. This being the aspect of bearing a grudge. And here they were commanded to avenge — the aspect of: "the sword of the avenging of the covenant." And all of this was preparation for the inheritance of Eretz Yisrael — which is from the aforementioned aspect.) And Elazar the priest said, etc., "this is the statute of the Torah," etc. Our Sages said: "he came to the point of error — for the laws of the gentile's vessels were forgotten from him," etc. For even though one needs the aspect of taking vengeance and bearing a grudge — through which specifically one can concentrate the light and divide the thousands into hundreds — even so one must be very careful from anger. For through it the light is entirely hidden, G-d forbid — (and if I erred, G-d forbid — He is merciful and will forgive). And this is: "for the blood of His servants He shall avenge — and He shall take vengeance against His enemies" — the aspect of taking vengeance and bearing a grudge, as stated above — and then: "and He shall atone for His land — His people." For this is related to the matter of the inheritance of Eretz Yisrael, as stated above. And this is: "for the day of vengeance is in my heart — and the year of My redemption has come." For this secret is relevant also to the matter of the drawing closer of the redemption. And this is what the verse concludes: "the smallest shall become a thousand — I am Hashem — in its time I will hasten it." And it is impossible to explain so much — and it is understood automatically.

 
 Sichot HaRan, Siman 97 · סימן צ"ז

 Ra'uy La-Adam — "It Is Fitting for a Person"

Eretz Yisrael is a foretaste of the World to Come — as stated above many times. And therefore there it is most fitting for a person to accustom himself to being in the World to Come — and to separate himself as much as possible from the animal desires of this world. And there one merits memory — as stated above many times. And therefore there it is easier to remind oneself of the delights of the World to Come. And regarding the matter of the three hundred and ten worlds that the Holy One Blessed be He will in the future bequeath to each and every Tzaddik — as it is written: "to bequeath to those who love Me — yesh." And it has already been explained above — what our Sages said: "'to those who love Me and keep My commandments' — these are the dwellers of Eretz Yisrael," etc. — and it is written: "and those who love His Name shall dwell in it." And see in Megaleh Amukos, aspect 62.

 Regarding the matter of what our Sages said: "one who dwells in Eretz Yisrael — it is as if he has a G-d" — they also allude to the reward of the future — to bequeath to those who love — yesh [three hundred and ten]. And the three hundred and ten worlds are built from dispute — this being the aspect of the dispute that was regarding the Patriarchs in the matter of Eretz Yisrael. As it is written: "and there was a quarrel between the herdsmen of Avram," etc. — and as Rashi explained. And similarly regarding Yitzchak: "and the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled," etc. And similarly regarding Yaakov: "and Esav hated him," etc. — until he was compelled to flee. And there: "and he heard the words of Lavan's sons" — and afterwards: "and Lavan overtook Yaakov," etc. — and: "and Yaakov was angry — and he quarreled with Lavan," etc. — and: "and Lavan answered," etc. — and: "and Yaakov said to his brothers: gather stones," etc. And afterwards — upon coming to Eretz Yisrael — the anger of Yosef leaped upon him. Meaning: the dispute that the tribes had with Yosef — which was a dispute of the Tzaddikim — as is explained within the ma'amar.

 And this is: "and he encountered the place — and lodged there," etc. — and the Zohar Chadash explained: from the language of complaint and quarrel. And: "and he took from the stones of the place," etc. — the aspect of the stones as is explained within the ma'amar. And there he was informed about the inheritance of Eretz Yisrael: "and Yaakov awoke," etc., "this is none other than the house of G-d," etc. — and: "and he called the name of that place Beis-El," etc., "and this stone," etc., "shall be the house of G-d," etc. For from these stones houses are built, etc. — as is explained within the ma'amar. And perhaps this is also the aspect of: "and all the congregation complained against Moshe and against Aharon" — which was through the spies — the spreaders of slander about the land — who disputed the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael itself. And there: "and all the congregation said: let us stone them with stones" — the aspect of the aforementioned stones — which are the letters of the words of the disputes. And placed adjacent to it afterwards: "when you come to the land of your dwelling," etc. — the aspect of the building of the houses and settlements made through the rectification of the aforementioned stones. And this is what our Sages expounded: "a land whose stones are iron" — do not read avanehah [its stones] but bonehah [its builders]. For they build houses from the aforementioned stones. And this too is the aspect of: "and great is the peace of your children — do not read banayich [your children] but bonayich [your builders]." For through the building of the houses — the aspect of shalom bayis [domestic peace] is made — as is explained within the ma'amar.

Sichot HaRan, Siman 102 · סימן ק"ב

 Shama'ti Be-Shemo — "I Heard in His Name"

 Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of emunah. And therefore it is called Eretz HaChayyim. For emunah is the primary of life — the aspect of: "and the righteous one shall live through his faith." And also there is the primary awe — as stated above many times — and therefore one merits there to length of days — the aspect of: "the awe of Hashem adds days." And also because there one merits complete faith — therefore teshuvah is easier. Meaning: one does not need to suffer so much pain and suffering to rectify the blemish. And this is: "and the inhabitant shall not say: I am sick — the people that dwells in it — their iniquity is forgiven." Meaning: through teshuvah alone — their sins are forgiven — even without illness and suffering, G-d forbid. The aspect of: "and what I sinned before You — cleanse through Your great compassion — but not through sufferings and bad illnesses, G-d forbid." As is explained within the ma'amar.

Sichot HaRan, Siman 110 · סימן ק"י

 Emunah — "Faith"

 Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of true wisdom — meaning: together with faith — which is called re'iyah [sight / vision] — as is explained within the ma'amar. And this is what is said: "and I saw the land" — and it is written: "lift your eyes and see," etc. And through this one is guarded from licentiousness — the aspect of: "I have made a covenant with my eyes," etc. And therefore Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of the tikkun of the bris — as is known.

Sichot HaRan, Siman 112 · סימן קי"ב

 Isa — "It Is Taught"

 Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — as is known. And therefore it is easier there to minimize sleep — which is the aspect of mochin d'katnus. And also one must be careful there as much as possible not to be a debtor. It is the aspect of mochin d'katnus — the aspect of sleep — the aspect of servitude — the aspect of: "the borrower is servant to the lender." And also there it is most propitious to repent in general — for all the sins — and among them also for the sin that causes one to be a debtor — and to bring many debtors into the world. And this is: "and you shall lend to many nations — and you shall not borrow," etc. And this is what is placed adjacent: "the wicked borrows and does not repay — and the righteous is gracious and gives — for those whom He blesses shall inherit the land," etc. For the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael is the opposite of the aspect of a debtor, as stated above.

Sichot HaRan, Siman 260 · סימן ר"ס

 VaYeshev Yaakov — "And Yaakov Dwelt"

 The primary perfection of faith one merits in Eretz Yisrael — as it is written: "dwell in the land and tend to faithfulness" — and Yerushalayim is called kiryah ne'emanah [a faithful city] — and this is: "our feet were standing in your gates, O Yerushalayim." The foot [regel] is the aspect of faith — as is explained within the ma'amar. And therefore from there — all the good influences and blessings — the aspect of: "a faithful man shall abound in blessings." And there is the primary lowliness and humility — as stated above many times. For Eretz Yisrael is in the aspect of the sanctity of Shabbos — through which one merits to see the lowliness and exaltedness of the Holy One Blessed be He, as stated above. And this is the aspect of: "and the humble shall inherit the land" — and it is written: "great is Hashem and greatly praised — in the city of our G-d," etc. — and it is written: "Hashem is great in Tzion — and exalted," etc. And there is the primary sweetening of the judgments, as stated above. And the primary rectification of the blemish of the moon. And therefore there is the primary mitzvah of the sanctification of the new month and the intercalation of years. And there is the primary union of the Name Havayah with the Name Elokim — as it is written: "and I returned in peace to the house of my father" — meaning: to Eretz Yisrael — "and Hashem shall be a G-d to me." And there is the primary mention of the Name Havayah in its writing — the aspect of: "in every place where I cause My Name to be remembered," etc. — and as our Sages said. For Eretz Yisrael — and in particular the Bais HaMikdash — is the aspect of the World to Come — wherein it will be called as it is written. And this is what our Sages said — that Yerushalayim itself will also be called by the Name of the Holy One Blessed be He — as it is written: "Hashem is there — Hashem Shamah."

 Parparos Na'eh, Part 1 · פרפראות נאה חלק א'

 Kesuvos 111 — Burial in Eretz Yisrael — The Gemara and Its Commentators

Kesuvos 111: "his brothers sent to Rabah: 'did Yaakov know' — he who was a complete Tzaddik," etc. See the discourse of Rabbi Shimon — Likutay Moharan Kama, Siman 61. And this is what they sent to Rabah: "did Yaakov know," etc. — meaning: since the primary resurrection of the dead will be only in Eretz Yisrael — and even Tzaddikim who are in the Diaspora will require the rolling of underground passages until they come to Eretz Yisrael — and there they will rise in resurrection. And all of this is because in the future — after the resurrection — Israel will receive very great souls. And the reception of the souls will be according to the aspect of the body. And therefore the bodies must also be in the aspect of the fruit of the land — in order to be able to receive great souls — as is explained within the ma'amar. And therefore the bodies must rise specifically in Eretz Yisrael — and then they will be very pure and holy bodies — and they will receive there great and exalted souls — the aspect of: "who gives a soul to the people upon it" — which our Sages expounded there. And because of this — even Yaakov our father — who was a complete Tzaddik — longed for burial in Eretz Yisrael. For through this the soul can illuminate within him even more — and he merits to receive aspects of very great and exalted levels. And as is also brought at length in the book Chesed Le-Avraham.

 And this is what they said there: "Ilfah adds to it matters — a story of one who suffered because of a certain one" — Rashi explained: "he fixed his eyes on her and she was in the Diaspora" — "and he wanted to descend — and once he heard this — he rolled himself until the day of his death." And from the language gilgel atzmo — it is understood that he could not take his mind off this pain all his days — and as is also understood in Chiddushay Aggados. It follows that he was at a very simple level. And even so he accepted upon himself all this pain until the day of his death. Meaning: in order to merit to die in Eretz Yisrael and be buried there — in order to merit at least after the resurrection to a holy body — and to receive a holy and elevated soul in level. And it is automatically understood from all of this — that they informed us that the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael encompasses from the top of all levels to the bottom of all levels. For even Yaakov our father longed for this. And from this it is understood that the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael is even more propitious for those who merit to dwell in it — and to receive great illuminations from the aspect of the soul — even in their living lives, as stated above. And similarly even very simple people in level — to the point that it is impossible for them to take their minds off the vanities of this world — even when they are dwelling in Eretz Yisrael. For there too their bodily corporeality overpowers them — and they cannot receive in fullness the illuminations of the soul. Even so — it is worth it and worth it — to endure everything — and to live there a life of pain — in corporeality and spirituality as well, G-d forbid — in order that at least they merit some completeness after the resurrection — as is understood from the story of the aforementioned man.

 (And there is also another manner of explanation — and there is no need to elaborate.) And this is: "even though you are a great sage — you have been found to have merited also there to receive a great illumination from the aspect of the soul." For the primary wisdom and understanding is through the soul — the aspect of: "and the breath of Shaddai shall give them understanding" — as is explained within the ma'amar. For in truth — through the sanctity of Israel — and in particular there in Babylon — where there were great Tzaddikim — and they spread much Torah there — therefore the air was also sanctified there — in the aspect of the sanctity of avira d'Eretz Yisrael machkim — and they also merited there to great souls — as is understood within the ma'amar. And therefore our Sages were indeed stringent about those who go out from Babylon to other lands. And they said: "one who dwells in Babylon — it is as if he dwells in Eretz Yisrael." It follows from all of this — you will say that you do not need to ascend to Eretz Yisrael. But in truth it is not so. For a student who learns from himself is not comparable to a student who learns from his master. And if you say: you have no master — you have a master — and who is it? — Rabbi Yochanan. Meaning: they informed him that even though he is a great sage — and merited to the aspect of a great soul — even so — his soul is only in the aspect of the particular intellect — which can sweeten only the contractions relevant to it. And even for the sweetening of these contractions alone — he also needs to receive strength and illumination from the aspect of the supernal wisdom — the all-encompassing intellect — where all the contractions are sweetened in general — and through this one merits in all one's matters — as is explained within the ma'amar. And therefore even a great sage — a student who learns from himself is not comparable to a student who learns from his master — who is the aspect of the all-encompassing intellect — supernal wisdom. And this is: and if you say: you have no master — only he himself is the master — the aspect of the all-encompassing intellect in this generation — for this he was told: you have a master — and who is it? — Rabbi Yochanan.

It follows that they informed him that he needs to ascend to Eretz Yisrael for two reasons. The first: because of the sanctity of Eretz Yisrael itself — where one merits to receive the illumination of the soul more greatly — which itself is the aspect of avira d'Eretz Yisrael machkim. Because there the light of supernal wisdom flows most greatly. For there is the point of the holy of holies — and the Even HaShetiyah — and: "for from Tzion Torah shall go forth", etc. — and as is explained elsewhere. And the second: because there he has a master — and who is it? — Rabbi Yochanan — who is the aspect of the all-encompassing intellect. This being the aspect of what our Sages said: "every rav in Babylon — and rabbi in Eretz Yisrael." And it is brought that the yud in the letters of rabbi alludes to the flowing of wisdom — which is the aspect of the all-encompassing intellect — which is the aspect of the springing fountain — the aspect of: "a flowing stream — the source of wisdom" — where everything is sweetened. And this is what is brought in the Tikkunim — Tikkun 22: "avira dachya — avira d'Eretz Yisrael de-ihi machkim — mi-sitra de-chochmah de-ihi yud" etc. And this is what they informed him at the outset also: "did Yaakov know," etc. For even Yaakov our father — who is himself the aspect of the totality of the souls of Israel — the aspect of the all-encompassing intellect — through which everything is sweetened — even so he longed for burial in Eretz Yisrael. And Ilfah adds — who informed him also from the complete opposite aspect. For even one who is very far from the sanctity of the intellect — all-encompassing — to the point where his intellect and soul have no power to sweeten any contraction and pain — and his mind is confused also in his dwelling in Eretz Yisrael — even so he too must strengthen himself greatly in the matter of dwelling in Eretz Yisrael — and endure everything — in order to merit through this to some good hope after the resurrection at least — as in the story of the aforementioned man.

 And this is: "and if you do not ascend — be careful of three things," etc. Meaning: they warned him at least — to hold on to every matter in the intermediate way — and not to tilt right or left — so that he should not fall through this to the aspect of surpluses, G-d forbid. This being the aspect of: "do not be overly righteous — and do not be overly wicked — and do not be overly wise" — and as is explained elsewhere. And because the entire order of a person's life is included in sitting and standing and walking — and as is explained in the commentators — regarding what Dovid the King, may peace be upon him, began his holy praises with: "praiseworthy is the man who has not walked", etc., "he has not stood", etc., "he has not sat" — therefore they warned him that in all these matters he should hold only to the intermediate way — the aspect of one-third standing — one-third sitting — one-third walking. And the intermediate is the aspect of the middle pillar — the aspect of justice — which one merits to through complete faith in the wise men — through which all the contractions are sweetened — and one merits complete counsel — and to bring forth true judgments from all the learnings one learns, etc. — as is explained within the ma'amar.

 And this is what they warned him: "do not increase sitting — for sitting is hard on the lower afflictions." And the primary pain and illness of the lower afflictions — which is the illness of hemorrhoids, G-d forbid — as is known — the primary intensification of pain and illness is at the time when he needs to relieve himself — meaning: to remove from himself the surpluses. Meaning: it begins at the lower end. For if one blemishes in faith in the wise men — and goes after one's own wisdom and intellect, G-d forbid — then one can fall into literal surpluses, G-d forbid — until it is very difficult to cleanse oneself from the surpluses — and it comes to him with great pain and great labor — the aspect of the lower afflictions, G-d forbid. And this is: "do not increase standing — for standing is hard on the heart." With this they alluded that sometimes the stench of the surpluses rises to the heart — where is the source of counsel — the aspect of: "deep waters — counsel in a person's heart." And it is written: "may He give you according to your heart — and may He fulfill all your counsel." And through the blemish of surpluses — one has no complete counsel forever — and he is always in doubt — and his heart is divided within him — for he cannot decide himself between the sides of his divided counsel. Which is itself also the aspect of standing — the aspect of: [Iyov 32] "for they stood — they did not answer anymore." For he does not know himself what to answer about the abundance of his doubts — and about the division of his counsel. This being the aspect of what the two sides of the disputing parties must stand — the aspect of: "and the two people who have the dispute shall stand," etc.

 (They also alluded to him that even those who engage in Torah — which is the aspect of sitting, as stated above — and also in prayer — which is the aspect of standing — as our Sages said — they must also be very careful in faith in the wise men — so that they should not fall, G-d forbid, into the aspect of surpluses. This being the aspect of what our Sages said: about the Torah of Doeg and Achitofel, etc. And similarly regarding prayer our Sages said: one who scrutinizes his prayer comes to heartache, etc.) And this is: "do not increase walking — for walking is hard on the eyes." Alluding that sometimes the fetid vapors of the surpluses rise to the brain — which is the aspect of eyes — for eyes — on account of wisdom they are mentioned — and through this the judgment is blemished — which is the aspect of: "it blinds the eyes of the wise." And the holy judgment — meaning: what one brings out from all the learnings that one learns — true judgments and upright conduct — these are the aspect of walking. For through this one knows the way to walk on it. This being the aspect of: "the ways of the world are His — do not read halichos [ways] but halachos [laws]." But through the blemish of faith in wise men — one falls into surpluses, G-d forbid — this being the aspect of: hard on the eyes. And then one is in the aspect of a fool walking in darkness, G-d forbid — for one cannot bring one's judgment to light. And this is what they concluded: "every sitting without ordination — standing with ordination is preferable to it." Meaning: for the primary rectification of the aspect of sitting — which is the aspect of wisdom of holiness — and standing — which is in the aspect of the holy contractions — all through ordination. Meaning: through ordaining a worthy master — who has complete faith in the wise men — for then through ordination — the light of the all-encompassing supernal intellect is drawn upon him. And through this he can sweeten all the contractions of all those close to him — and rectify their counsel in fullness — and instruct them in true judgments and upright conduct. But sitting without ordination — meaning: a sage and leader such as this — who is not worthy to receive the illumination of the ordination — then standing with ordination — meaning: it is better to receive the divided counsel and the doubts in the halachah — of worthy and God-fearing people — who have complete faith in the wise men — through which the primary ordination operates — for then he has some hope — to rectify his counsel somewhat — and to walk on a straight path — through the doubts and the division of counsel themselves. Which is not so if he accepts counsel and halachos from an unworthy master — who is not worthy for ordination — then he will have no doubt at all — and his counsel will be completely corrupted. And this is the aspect of: "praiseworthy is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked" — corresponding to the corruption of counsel. "And in the way of sinners has not stood" — corresponding to the blemish of judgment — the aspect of [Nechemiah 9]: "and in Your judgments they sinned." "And in the assembly of scorners has not sat" — corresponding to the blemish of the scorners of the words of the wise men — through which one is judged through surpluses, as stated above. And this is: "but his desire is in the Torah of Hashem." And our Sages expounded: "a person should always learn Torah from whom he desires — and in what his heart desires." For from there presumably is the root of his soul and the sweetening of his contractions. And this is: "and in His Torah he meditates day and night." Meaning: he engages to innovate in Torah at every time — and has faith in the wise men even in his own innovations — and all the more so in the true innovations of all the authentic Torah scholars — and through this the light of the Torah is completed even more — and then the Torah is called his Torah — as our Sages expounded. And see [Avodah Zarah 19]. And this is: "and he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water." For this flows through the aspect of: "a portion of G-d — full of water" — as is explained within the ma'amar. And in truth — the perfection of the rectification of counsel and the rectification of judgment are in one aspect — the aspect of: "and I shall restore your judges as at first — and your counselors," etc. And even so — they are two aspects — (and this is not the place to elaborate).

And behold — the matter of sitting and standing and walking — as stated above — can be explained further in many modes. And however it may be — in any case — they alluded to him that if he does not wish to ascend to Eretz Yisrael — where the primary illumination of the all-encompassing supernal intellect — the source of life — shines — and in particular since Rabbi Yochanan is there, as stated above — therefore at least let him guard his soul from things that blemish life — and are derived from the aspect of surpluses — that come through the inability to sweeten the contractions as is fitting. From which is derived and comes also in corporeality — the illness of the lower afflictions, G-d forbid. And illness of the heart — corresponding to the aspect of the blemish of counsel. And the ruination of the eyes — corresponding to the blemish of judgment — that comes from the brain, as stated above. And this is what they concluded: "and similarly Yitzchak and Shimon and Oshaiah said the same thing — the law follows Rabbi Yehudah in the matter of separations." [Rashi explained: it is uncertain to him whether one is concerned about the seed of the father, etc.] See Ma'oray Or: "asher pared im ha-kollel — in gematria — mantzepach [the final letters] together with the letters." For from there the judgments grasp in separation. And see in the Introduction to the Tikkunim — that wisdom is called the father of faith. It follows that faith is the aspect of the seed of the father. And through the blemish of faith in the wise men — a separation is made between faith and wisdom — as is explained elsewhere. And therefore — when a person sees that dispute comes upon him — which is the aspect of division of hearts — he must suspect himself: perhaps he blemished in faith in the wise men — through which the contractions cannot be sweetened — and through this dispute and division are made. Therefore he must repent on this — and rectify the blemish of faith in the wise men — and as is explained within the ma'amar.

 
 Parparos Na'eh, Part 2 · פרפראות נאה חלק ב'

 Maharyit — Rabbeinu Chananel — Halachic Discussion

See in the novellae of the Maharyit on Kesuvos — brought there in the name of Rabbeinu Chananel — who explained: "the law follows Rabbi Yehudah in the matter of separations." Meaning: one is not concerned about the seed of the father. And he alludes to the matter of the one from the house of Eli, etc. — see there what he was precise about. And see Chullin 79 — the plain meaning of the language of the Gemara is also thus. And see in the Rif and the Ran there — and you will understand better. And according to the above — the matter is explained — both according to the view of Rashi and according to the view of Rabbeinu Chananel, of blessed memory. For our Sages said [Sanhedrin 14]: "there is no ordination outside the land," etc. And there they said the matter that those from the house of Eli are not ordained — as it is said: "there shall not be an elder in your house all the days," etc. — see there. It follows: perhaps Rabah would say — since he comes from the house of Eli — and those from there are not ordained — it follows that they are in the aspect of the Diaspora — where the light of supernal wisdom does not flow — from which the root of ordination comes — therefore he has no need to strive to come to Eretz Yisrael. Therefore they alluded to him that one is not concerned about the seed of the father in this — and certainly he too can receive there the illumination of supernal wisdom — and in particular through Rabbi Yochanan. And see there further — [Shmuel I, chapters 2, 3, 4] — regarding the matter of the sons of Eli — who through their blemishing in the honor of the sanctuary and its holy things — where the light of wisdom flows — the aspect of holy — therefore they were punished — that there would be from among them no high priest who enters the holy of holies — to draw from there the sweetening of the contractions through wisdom and faith. And this is: "and you shall behold a rival in all that He shall benefit Israel." This will be through the sweetening of the contractions — through the light of wisdom that flows in the Bais HaMikdash — and to them it will be distress and pain — even in the very sanctuary of the Temple — for they will see their distress — in that no high priest is appointed from among them. It follows that for them the Temple itself will be in the aspect of contraction and distress — because of the sweetening. And this is: "measure for measure." And this is: "and there shall not be an elder in your house," etc. — that they will not be ordained, as stated above. And this is: "and one I will not cut off from My altar — to cause your eyes to fail and to grieve your soul." This being the aspect of the illness of the lower afflictions — as is brought above in the name of our Sages' exposition. And: "and all the multitude of your house shall die as young men." The opposite of life and length of days — that flows through wisdom, as stated above. And see there further — afterwards — regarding the matter of the Philistine wars that were aroused against them. For this came from the aspect of the overpowering of contractions and judgments so greatly — until the Ark of G-d was taken — where are the tablets of stone — from which one draws the sweetening of contractions through wisdom and faith. And now — because of the sin of the house of Eli — the contractions overpowered so greatly — until the Ark of G-d too was taken — and then the two sons of Eli died — and also Eli the priest died. And this is the aspect of: "the glory has been exiled from Israel," etc. For glory alludes to the thirty-two paths of wisdom — as is known. And this is: "the glory of the wise they shall inherit." And this is: "for the Ark of G-d was taken." And afterwards Hashem struck the Philistines with the plague of hemorrhoids — which is the illness of the lower afflictions — as is explained there in the commentators — until they were forced to return the Ark.

 
 Parparos Na'eh, Part 3 · פרפראות נאה חלק ג'

 Rashi's View — Halachic Continuation

And according to the view of Rashi — that the law follows Rabbi Yehudah — and it is uncertain to him whether one is concerned about the seed of the father, etc. — it will be explained also in this manner. For on the contrary — since the family of Rabah is from the house of Eli — one must certainly strive and rectify this — and come to Eretz Yisrael — and accept before Rabbi Yochanan his master. In order that through this he merit to draw upon himself the supernal sweetening from the aspect of supernal wisdom — until he be saved from all the above. And perhaps he will merit through this to length of days. And therefore — the Tosafos indeed wrote — in truth — [Eruvin 24, Yevamos 78] — that Rabah ascended to Eretz Yisrael and accepted before Rabbi Yochanan. (And see Seder HaDoros — what he deliberated regarding this.)
